title: Enterprise requirements gathering: auditability + immutability for model changelog (Console + docs mapping)
creator: Marissa Cole
project: Model Metadata Schema + Customer-visible Model Changelog (v1)
description:
## Context
Multiple enterprise prospects/customers have asked for (1) immutable model release notes and (2) auditable history of changes (who/what/when) to satisfy internal change-management and regulatory obligations.

This issue gathers enterprise requirements and maps them to:
- Model registry schema + change-event design (source of truth)
- Changelog generator workflow (draft/in_review/published + corrections)
- Console customer experience (what is visible, what is exportable)
- Docs customer experience (what we commit to publicly)

## Why this matters
We are getting blocked in security/procurement reviews because our current model update communication is inconsistent and not provably tamper-evident. This is also driving support escalations when customers claim behavior changed without notice.

Notable inputs:
- SUP-18421 (enterprise request: immutable model release notes + audit trail + export)
- FinchBank security review (Fireflies 2026-02-11) and HubSpot notes
- Security/Compliance asks: retention policy language, RBAC, and evidence of non-repudiation

## Goals / Output
By end of this ticket we should have:
1) A written set of enterprise requirements (must/should) for auditability + immutability.
2) Clear mapping of each requirement to a system surface:
   - Console UI and API
   - Public docs (what we promise)
   - Internal audit logs / SIEM export
3) Open questions resolved (or explicitly deferred) with owners.

## Enterprise requirements (draft)
### A. Immutability / tamper-evidence
MUST:
- Published changelog entries are immutable to customers.
- Corrections are handled by "superseding" (create a new entry that points to the prior entry) rather than editing in place.
- Every entry has stable identifiers (entry_id, event_id, model_id, version_id) and timestamps.
- Ability to show evidence that entries were not altered after publication (hash/signature and storage controls). Customer does not need raw cryptographic primitives in UI, but we must be able to answer security questionnaires.

SHOULD:
- Provide a signed JSON feed (or at least documented hash) for customers who archive entries.

### B. Auditability / provenance
MUST:
- Track and retain who changed model metadata that affects customer-visible output (actor, time, diff summary, approval chain).
- Track and retain who approved and who published the customer-visible entry.
- Maintain history across environments (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) with consistent semantics.

SHOULD:
- Export audit events to customer SIEM for Private deployments (and at least internal SIEM for Hosted/Dedicated).

### C. Retention
MUST:
- Define retention duration for:
  - customer-visible changelog entries
  - internal audit events backing those entries
- Retention must be documented for enterprise contracts and questionnaires.

Proposed baseline to validate with GRC:
- Customer-visible published entries: retain indefinitely (or minimum 7 years) while model/version is supported + at least 24 months after sunset.
- Internal audit events: minimum 7 years (Hosted/Dedicated) with immutable storage controls.

### D. Access control / approvals
MUST:
- RBAC separation:
  - who can edit model metadata
  - who can move release notes to in_review
  - who can publish
- Approval workflow is explicit (draft -> in_review -> published) with timestamps.
- Emergency path for urgent corrections/hotfixes is documented and still produces an auditable trail.

### E. Customer UX (Console + docs)
MUST (Console):
- Customers can view per-model and per-version release notes with published timestamps.
- Customers can see deprecation timelines and replacement guidance.
- Customers can obtain a stable link (per entry) and export options suitable for change-management processes.

MUST (Docs):
- Public documentation states:
  - that release notes are generated from a single source of truth
  - that published entries are not edited; corrections are superseded
  - where to subscribe (RSS/JSON feed) and how to interpret “corrected” entries

SHOULD:
- Provide a machine-readable feed with ETags + pagination (for customer change-control automation).

## Mapping (initial)
- Immutability: registry change-events + generator storing published artifacts; corrections via supersede (ENG work). Docs should explicitly state our correction model.
- Auditability: audit event spec (Security/Compliance) + role checks in publish endpoints; Console should show “Published by Redwood” but NOT leak internal usernames unless policy allows.
- Retention: Security to confirm storage + retention; Product to ensure language in docs/enterprise collateral.

## Open questions
1) Do we expose any actor identity to customers (e.g., “Redwood Release Engineering” vs individual)? Proposed: team-level only.
2) What is the canonical retention statement we can commit to publicly (indefinite vs 7 years)? Need GRC sign-off.
3) For Private/on-prem: is customer expected to host the changelog store, or do we ship signed bundles? (likely v1: Private gets same APIs; on-prem gets packaged service with local storage + optional export)
4) Do we need customer-specific feeds (per account) for Dedicated/Private? Proposed: out of scope v1.

## Deliverables
- 1-pager requirements summary (Confluence link to be added)
- Table mapping requirements -> implementation surface (Console/API/Docs/Audit logs)
- Final decision on retention language + actor identity policy

## Success metric
Unblocks FinchBank/HelioHealth-style security reviews and reduces back-and-forth in questionnaires (measured qualitatively for beta + via sales cycle notes).

comments: 2026-01-28 (Marissa Cole): Pulling together enterprise questionnaire asks we’ve seen repeatedly (immutability, retention, SIEM export). Naomi + Marcus/Olga—can you confirm what retention we can safely commit to in public docs vs contract-only language?

2026-02-03 (Naomi Feldman): From Compliance POV, we should avoid promising “indefinite” unless we can operationally guarantee it. Recommend: published release notes retained for at least 7 years, and internal audit events retained for at least 7 years, with the option to extend for regulated customers. Also: do not expose individual employee identities in customer UI; show a role (e.g., “Release Engineering”).

2026-02-05 (Connor O'Brien): +1 on supersede-not-edit. For release engineering, we need an emergency correction path that still records the old entry and links forward. Also: we should align with freeze windows—publishing during RC should be allowed but require explicit approver.

2026-02-11 (Marcus Lin): Immutability should be framed as “tamper-evident” + “append-only” rather than absolute immutability. We can meet enterprise expectations via WORM-capable storage and signed events; actual implementation specifics shouldn’t be in public docs, but we need an internal control statement and an answer for questionnaires.

2026-02-14 (Wei Chen): For docs, we need a short, clear statement: (1) entries are generated from registry events, (2) entries aren’t edited; corrections are published as new entries, (3) each entry has a stable URL and timestamp, (4) feed subscription guidance. Please confirm actor identity policy before we draft UI screenshots.

2026-02-18 (Naomi Feldman): Proposed final stance: customers see “Published by: Redwood Release Engineering” (or “Redwood”) and “Approved by: Redwood” without individuals. Internally we retain full actor identifiers in audit events. Waiting on Olga for retention language sign-off.
updates: 2026-02-06: Collected inputs from SUP-18421 + FinchBank call; consolidated into MUST/SHOULD list in description.
2026-02-12: Added mapping notes for Console vs Docs vs Audit log surfaces; flagged actor-identity and retention as open questions.
2026-02-18: Tentative decision: no individual actor identity exposed to customers; role-based display only. Pending GRC approval on retention language.
acceptance_criteria: Requirements list (MUST/SHOULD) reviewed by Security (Marcus Lin) and GRC (Olga Petrov) and marked final.
Retention language approved for: public docs wording + enterprise questionnaire response snippet.
Decision recorded for actor identity exposure (customer UI + docs).
Mapping table produced: each enterprise requirement -> Console behavior, Docs behavior, API/feed behavior, and internal audit logging behavior.
Any out-of-scope items explicitly documented with rationale and follow-up issue(s).
risks: Over-promising retention/immutability in public docs creates contractual expectations we can’t meet operationally.
If corrections allow in-place editing, enterprise trust/auditability will fail; needs strict supersede behavior.
If Console exposes too much internal detail (actors/vendor/model nicknames), we may leak internal-only metadata.
